![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/9b328ecd6017922e429f11c57aca0ff452e4dc6a1476b14a448c6c9edd6b6679.png)

Consider the region bounded by $x=2-\sqrt{y}$ and $y=1-{x}^{2}$  from $y=0$ to $y=1,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our second function in terms of $y,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}y=1-{x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{1-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(y)=2-\sqrt{y}$ and $g(y)=\sqrt{1-y}.$

Let's draw our horizontal arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/7d92b9f69ab27a2620ae94bfb4937509fc9db6dafdec4384af5de33a4dfecd30.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $x=g(y)=\sqrt{1-y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $x=f(y)=2-\sqrt{y}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[2-\sqrt{y}]}^{2}-{[\sqrt{1-y}]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[2-\sqrt{y}]}^{2}-{[\sqrt{1-y}]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
